title: Lupus SS test
bodyHtml:
The Signal Sifter allows you to view lupus-associated variants in a genomic region of interest, from an analysis of 7,219 SLE cases and 15,991 controls of European ancestry (Bentham, Morris, et al., 2015), in the context of thousands of tissue-specific genomic annotations. View associations across the genome in the section below to identify a region of interest, or go straight to a region by entering a gene name or genomic coordinates (in the format "chr:start-end", e.g. "6:25413381-34403276") below. In each section, clicking on the "camera" icon at the upper right will capture the data in that section and offer the opportunity to create a downloadable summary table in the Summary Section.
The plot and table display gene-level associations for SLE with p-value ≤ 0.05, as determined by the MAGMA method.

Explore genetic associations for SLE on the Associated Variants (Single Phenotype) tab, which displays LD-clumped genome-wide significant (p ≤ 5e-8) associations across the genome, or the Associated Genes tab, which displays gene-level associations. The Summary tab combines information from both tabs into a single table.

Use the filters above to filter both the plot and table. After identifying a genomic region of interest, mouse over a genomic region in the table and click Set region to view more details about the region in the sections below.

This section displays LD-clumped SLE genetic associations in the region you have selected. Filter both the plot and table using the filters below. 
Clumped Variants description
Global Enrichment description
The tracks and table below display tissue-specific epigenomic annotations in this region, drawn from the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA). To see annotations in specific biosamples within a tissue, mouse over a tissue name in the table, click on Set tissue, and then view the Enriched Biosamples in Region tab.
The tracks and table below display cell type (biosample)-specific epigenomic annotations in this region for the tissue(s) you have set.
The tracks in this section display genomic regions that are linked to specific genes by 3-D chromatin interactions in the tissue(s) you have set, discovered by techniques such as ChIP-seq or Hi-C.
The tracks in this section display genomic regions that are linked to specific genes by the Combined SNP-to-Gene strategy (Gazal et al., 2022). These links are not tissue-specific.
